Through: Mr Yasir Rauf Ansari, ASC for Stat  Adeeb-ul-Hasan, Adv.
 Inspector Sandeep Kumar, PS-Vasant  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JASMEET SINGH  ORDER % 20.01.2023 1.
This is a petition seeking quashing of FIR No. 330/2014 dated 18.04.2014, under Sections 420/468 IPC, registered at Police Station-Vasant Vihar, New Delhi.

2. As per the FIR, it is stated that the petitioner No.3 in conspiracy with petitioner Nos. 1 and other officials of petitioner No. 2 forged a letter of guarantee of the complainant/respondent No.2 by forging his signatures on 27.01.2011 and took a loan for a sum of Rs. 20 lakhs.
In addition, on the letter of guarantee, the photographs and the details of the complainant/respondent No.2 were also submitted.
His PAN card was also annexed with the complaint.
Hence the FIR.
3. The respondent-State has filed a status report wherein they have come to a conclusion that the letter of guarantee of respondent No.2 was forged.
4. The present quashing is predicated on a settlement dated 02.10.2021 between the petitioners and respondent No.2.
5. Petitioner No.2 is present in Court and is also representing petitioner No.1

He is identified by Mr Karnail Singh, Adv.
6.
The respondent No.2/complainant is also present in Court and has been identified by the Investigation Officer Inspector Sandeep Kumar, PS- Vasant Vihar.

sentences.text: The petitioners and respondent No.2 state that they have entered into the aforesaid settlement out of their own free will, volition and without any threat, pressure, undue influence or coercion.
Respondent No.2 states that he does not wish to prosecute his complaint and he has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

8. Even though respondent No.2 does not wish to prosecute the complaint against petitioner No.3 also, however, I am of the view that the FIR against petitioner No.3 is not liable to be quashed as of now.
Evidence is required to be led as to how the guarantee was forged.
9. As per the status report, the letter of guarantee was forged and a fabricated document.
The petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 have also suffered as they have parted with Rs. 20 lakhs relying on the letter of guarantee.

10. Hence, I am of the view that the FIR should be quashed qua petitioner Nos. 1 and 2.
11.

The partial quashing of the FIR is also permissible in accordance with Lovely Salhotra v. State (NCT of Delhi), (2018) 12 SCC 391:
"3.

entities.text: Lovely Salhotra v. State (NCT of Delhi), (2018) 12 SCC 391
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have taken into account the facts of the matter in question as it appears to us that no cognizable offence is made out against the appellants herein.

The High Court was wrong in holding that the FIR cannot be quashed in part and it ought to have appreciated the fact that the appellants herein cannot be allowed to suffer on the basis of the complaint filed by Respondent 2 herein only on the ground that the investigation against co-accused is still pending.
It is pertinent to note that the learned Magistrate has opined that no offence is made out against Co-accused 2, 3, 4 and 6 prima facie.

According to us, the FIR in question filed against the appellants herein by Respondent 2 is only an afterthought with the sole intention to pressurise the appellants not to prosecute their criminal complaint filed by them under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
4.

Accordingly, we find that the order [Lovely Salhotra v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2016 SCC OnLine Del 6583] so passed by the High Court is not sustainable in the eye of the law and deserves to be set aside.

entities.text: Lovely Salhotra v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2016 SCC OnLine Del 6583
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, we set aside the said order of the High Court and quash the FIR qua the appellants herein.

The appeal is allowed in the aforestated terms."
12.

This court in CRL. M.C. 1741/2021, titled SUNIL TOMAR v. THE STATE OF NCT OF DELHI &
ANR vide order dated APRIL 12, 2022

entities.text:
SUNIL TOMAR v. THE STATE OF NCT OF DELHI &
ANR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
also observed:
"Partial quashing or part quashing of FIR only qua the petitioner/accused with whom the complainant has compromised or settled the matter can be allowed and while quashing, it must be appreciated that the petitioner/accused cannot be allowed to suffer based on a complaint filed by the respondent, when subsequently, all disputes have been settled between the parties."

sentences.text:
For the reasons stated above and based on the settlement, FIR No. 330/2014 dated 18.04.2014,
under Sections 420/468 IPC, registered at Police Station-Vasant Vihar, New Delhi and proceedings pursuant thereto, if any, are hereby quashed against petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 only.

14. Mr Sumit Goswami, learned counsel appearing on behalf of petitioner No.3 states that even though there is no application seeking protection from arrest but as the matter has been settled, the petitioner No.3 may be granted protection from arrest.
15. Mr Rauf, learned ASC on instruction states that the FIR is of the year 2014, the investigation has been completed and there is no requirement of petitioner No.3 for custodial interrogation.
16. The very fact that the petitioner No.3 has not been arrested for 9 years shows that there is no requirement of arrest of the petitioner No.3.

Be that as it may, it is directed that subject to the petitioner No.3 appearing before the Investigating Officer and before the Court as and when required, the petitioner No.3 shall not be arrested in FIR No. 330/2014 dated 18.04.2014, under Sections 420/468 IPC, registered at Police Station-Vasant Vihar, New Delhi.
17. The petition is disposed of in the above terms.
JASMEET SINGH, J JANUARY 20, 2023/sr
